http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/23/.text: World / Europe One dead, several injured in Czech army helicopter crash Published: 23 Jul 2026 - 04:10 pm | Last Updated: 23 Jul 2026 - 04:10 pm AFP Prague: One person died and several were injured on Thursday when a military helicopter crashed in the Czech Republic with five soldiers on board, the army and emergency services said. "A Venom helicopter has crashed at the 22nd helicopter base in Namest nad Oslavou. Five soldiers were on board. Emergency services are currently deployed at the scene," the army wrote on X. Petr Janacek, a spokesman for the Vysocina regional rescue services, told AFP that one of the passengers was found dead and three were taken to hospitals in the region, two of them with "moderately serious injuries". A rescue operation was still under way, he said. No information was immediately available regarding the fifth soldier. The Namest and Oslavou airbase is located around 200 kilometres (125 miles) southeast of Prague. Police were informed of the accident at 12:11pm (1011 GMT), regional police spokeswoman Dana Cirtkova told the CTK news agency. Defence Minister Jaromir Zuna said the incident was "an immense tragedy that affects us all deeply", adding that an inquiry was under way to determine the cause of the crash. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: As many as 141 people are thought to have died trying to cross from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta at the end of July and the start of August. Photograph: Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen As many as 141 people are thought to have died trying to cross from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta at the end of July and the start of August. Photograph: Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP/Getty Images Spain Morocco not to blame for Ceuta border breach, says Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez says two countries are cooperating after mass incursion by 70,000 people into north African enclave Sam Jones in Madrid Mon 31 Aug 2026 06.21 EDT Last modified on Mon 31 Aug 2026 06.23 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has insisted there was no evidence to suggest the Moroccan government was behind last month’s massive border crossing into Ceuta . As many as 141 people are thought to have died trying to enter the Spanish enclave at the end of July. The influx of about 70,000 men, women and children unleashed a political crisis, a humanitarian emergency and reignited tensions over immigration within the EU . Although the overwhelming majority of the migrants crossed back into Morocco weeks ago , hundreds of people, including minors, are still on the streets of Ceuta, leading to tensions with residents. Despite speculation that Rabat may have engineered the mass crossing as a means of showing its displeasure at Spain’s rapprochement with Algeria , Sánchez said there was nothing to indicate the involvement of the Moroccan authorities. “There’s no information from any intelligence agency that raises doubts over the involvement of Moroccan authorities,” he told Cadena Ser radio on Monday. “Cooperation with Morocco is frankly positive. I’d like to stress that we need to be aware that this crisis can be resolved only through cooperation – and not through a lack of trust in Morocco, which would only further aggravate the already complex situation we have in Ceuta.” ‘We want to find a better future’: teenage girls on why they risked their lives to reach Spain Read more The prime minister once again pointed the finger at “criminal gangs” who had used disinformation to falsely claim that a ruling by Spain’s supreme court meant that no one who entered Ceuta by swimming could be deported back to Morocco. View image in fullscreen Pedro Sánchez says about 1,500 migrants remain in Ceuta after the border breach. Photograph: Jaime Reina/AFP/Getty Images He also said fake news had been pumped out on social media accounts “associated with Russia, Israel and the international far right that always use migration to attack not just Spain but also Europe”. Sánchez said that about 1,500 migrants remained in Ceuta, of whom 1,200 are minors, and there would soon be “sufficient capacity” to accommodate all those still in the enclave. Their continuing presence has led to clashes between some Ceuta residents and police, while some of the migrants have had their belongings burned while sleeping rough on beaches. On Saturday, four Moroccan migrants were arrested for throwing stones at Spanish soldiers. Spain’s conservative People’s party has accused the government of failing to protect the people of Ceuta. “It did nothing to avoid the invasion on 30 July and it’s doing nothing to stop the public order crisis that’s getting worse every day,” the PP’s leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, said last week. Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, has described events in Ceuta as “an invasion and an act of war promoted by Morocco and allowed by Sánchez, who is incapable of responding because he is subservient to Morocco”. https://www.dw.com/en/saudi-arabia-says-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Mffv The Saudi-Houthi conflict has opened up another front in the ongoing Middle East war Image: Fayez Nureldine/AFP Advertisement Saudi Arabia said on Wednesday that its air defenses had intercepted and destroyed a drone allegedly launched by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis before it entered restricted airspace over Islam's holiest city Mecca. The Houthis denied targeting the city, which is the destination of the annual Muslim hajj pilgrimage. The claim was announced by the Joint Forces Command of what is still called the Saudi-led coalition. The multinational alliance formed in 2015 has largely fragmented, leaving current operations dominated by Saudi Arabia and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the security of Mecca and its pilgrims was a "red line" and warned that the command would take "necessary and deterrent measures." According to the statement, the Royal Saudi Air Defense Forces intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone "launched by the Terrorist Houthi Militia." Saudi Arabia had issued brief alerts on Tuesday over possible attacks in Mecca and in the kingdom's southern region which borders Yemen. How did the Houthis respond? The Houthis were quick to reject the coalition's claims as a "lie." "The claims about targeting Mecca are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone," Hazem al-Assad, a high-ranking member from the Houthi movement, wrote on X. Pakistan's prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, condemned "in the strongest possible terms the dastardly and heinous attack on Mecca." "The people of Pakistan are saddened and perturbed by this outrageous act," he wrote on X. Houthis seize Red Sea chokepoint: What can Saudi Arabia do? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Meanwhile, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), a bloc of 57 Muslim nations, also condemned the "henious" attack. The OIC General Secretariat "stresses that the violation of the sanctity of the holy sites is an unacceptable and intolerable transgression that requires deterring the perpetrators and blocking the path of anyone who dares to infringe upon these sites," it said in a statement. Why are Saudi forces in conflict with the Houthis? Saudi Arabia is being increasingly affected by the rapidly escalating conflict across its southern border in Yemen, where the Iran-backed Houthis are fighting Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces. Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia injured 13 people on Monday night, bringing the total number of people injured since the conflict escalated in July to about 100. In July, the Houthis also blocked Saudi oil shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, that had been serving as an alternative route for Saudi oil exports amid Iran's blockade of the nearby Strait of Hormuz. Houthi attacks in Yemen open dangerous new Middle East front To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video With the kingdom under attack, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Tuesday reached out to Egypt for support against Yemen's Houthi rebels. The leaders called for "ensuring the freedom and security of maritime navigation" through Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab — which links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. The growing escalation has opened up another front in the Middle East, which is already grappling with the US war on Iran. Amid the latest development, the US Embassy in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday issued an advisory asking its citizens to "reconsider travel" to the kingdom. It warned of the "risk of Iranian drone and missile targeting American interests, armed conflict, terrorism, exit bans and local laws regarding social media activity." https://telex.hu/sport/2026/09/25/magyor.text: Menü Kereső A magyar válogatott kikapott Ukrajnától, majd a meccs végén egymásnak ugrott a két csapat Sport Fehér János Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A magyar futballválogatott rengeteg helyzetet összehozott a Puskás Arénában, de 1-0-ra kikapott Ukrajnától a Nemzetek Ligája B divíziójának első fordulójában. A mérkőzés utolsó percei botrányos jeleneteket hoztak, egymásnak esett a két csapat. A magyar válogatott idei első tétmérkőzését játszotta, ami előtt nem volt könnyű helyzetben Marco Rossi szövetségi kapitány. Sérülések miatt több veszélyes támadóról, mint Varga Barnabásról vagy Sallai Rolandról is le kellett mondania , de rajtuk kívül más alapemberek, mint Dibusz Dénes, Callum Styles vagy Dárdai Márton is hiányoztak a keretből . A támadósorba végül Lukács Dániel és Demir Redzic került, mögöttük természetesen Szoboszlai Dominik irányított. Az ukránok agilisen kezdtek, magasra tolták fel a védekezésüket, és az első néhány percben nehezen jött ki a szorításból a magyar csapat. Egy ritmusváltás után viszont már az ukránoknak kellett rendezniük a védelmüket, sorra jöttek a magyar támadások. Igaz, egy ukrán kontra Schäfer András felesleges szabálytalanságát és az első sárga lapot hozta a meccs elején. Hektikus játékkép alakult ki, mind a két csapat kockázatot és erős iramot felvállalva támadott, de az első nagy helyzet a magyar csapaté volt. A 11. percben Szoboszlai tette be középre a labdát, ahonnan Lukács kapásból, félfordulatból tűzte kapura. A lövése váratlan volt, és mivel a felső lécen csattant, fellélegezhettek az ukránok. Nem sokkal később Danyilo Szikan került lövőhelyzetbe, de vagy másfél méterrel elkerülte a kísérlete a kaput. Lukács Dániel félfordulatos lövése – Fotó: Szabó Bernadett / Reuters A 19. percben aztán Bolla Bendegúz hagyott ki egy ziccert. Először Szoboszlai lőtt, de azt kivédekezték az ukránok, a magyar csapatkapitányhoz viszont visszakerült a labda, és bejátszotta az üresen maradt Bollának, aki öt méterről sem találta el a kaput. Fájhatott a feje, de Schäfernek ténylegesen is, mert Volodimir Brazskó két perccel később fejbe rúgta. Ápolás után azért tudta folytatni a játékot a magyar középpályás. A játék továbbra is intenzív volt, de az ukránok sem jutottak el kapura lövésig az első fél órában, leszámítva egy leshelyzetet, de Tóth Balázs azt a lövést is védte. A hol bal oldalon, hol jobb oldalon feltűnő Szoboszlai próbálta áthelyezni a támadások súlypontját, de az ukránok jól levédekezték ezeket és a gyors átmenetekben is jók voltak. A 38. percben aztán Szoboszlai szerzett labdát az ukrán térfél közepén, majd ki is tette balra Kerkeznek, aki kicsit kiszorított helyzetből lőtt. Két perccel később megint Szoboszlai indult meg, majd a 16-oson belül elesett. Büntetőt reklamált, de a játékvezető nem fújta le, és a videóbírók sem erősítették meg, hogy szabálytalanság történt volna. Ezután az ukránok percei jöttek, Csongvai még blokkolni tudta Brazsko lövését a kapu előtt, a következő támadásnál viszont már rövidzárlat volt a védelemben. A 42. percben a bal szélről Szudakov tekerte be középre a labdát, amire védők által teljesen üresen hagyott Szikan csapott le, és fejelt a kapuba 7 méterről. Csinger lekövette az egyik bemozgó játékost, Kerkez viszont nem követte le Szikant. A magyar csapat a 45. percben még esélyt kapott az egyenlítésre, egy szöglet utáni tumultusban próbálták a kapuba gyömöszölni a labdát, de nem találta meg a rést. Az ukránok első gólját Danyilo Szikan szerezte fejjel – Fotó: Szabó Bernadett / Reuters A második félidőre Rossi a támadójátékon próbált meg változtatni, Bárány Donátot Lukács helyére hozta be, míg az újonc Tóth Milán a nem túl sokat mutató Vitális Milán helyére került. Míg az első félidőben inkább a jobb szélen vezette a támadásait a válogatott, Tóth beállása után a bal oldalt is aktivizálták, a 49. percben egy Szoboszlai-sarkazással indított szép akció meg is zavarta az ukránokat, csak szabálytalanul tudták megállítani Tóthot, majd a következő támadás magyar szögletet hozott. Az 55. percben Tóth aztán nagy helyzetig is jutott, egy visszafejelt labdát lőhetett kapura 14 méterről, de erőtlen lett kísérlete, Riznik kapus könnyedén ölre vette a lövést. Schäfer egy távoli lapos lövéssel próbált meg veszélyeztetni, de ezzel sem lehetett meglepni Rizniket. Az ukránok nem erőltették a támadásokat ebben a szakaszban, látványosan átengedték a területet a magyar válogatottnak, és már csak kontrákra építették a taktikájukat. Rossi még egyet módosított a támadósoron, Redzic helyére a szintén újonc Jurek Gábort cserélte be bő egyórányi játék után. A kicsit leülő meccs aztán a 69. percben kapott újra szikrát, egy jobb oldalon végigfutó akció után Jurek egy jó csellel elküldte a védőjét, és középre is tudott emelni. Kerkez középen elesett, büntető reklamált, de a bíró nem fújt, miközben Szoboszlai folyamatosan kereste a lövőhelyzetet. Az ukránok végül csak nehézkesen jöttek ki a szorításból. A következő percek a magyar letámadásokról és labdaszerzésekről szóltak, Ukrajna nagy nyomás alá került, de azért igazán jó helyzethez nem juttatták Szoboszlaiékat. A 77. percben az ukránok vezettek hosszú idő után támadást, nagy energiákat ebbe sem öltek, de aztán Krasznopir kapott egy remek kiugrást, és egyedül vihette kapura. Tóth jól jött ki a kapujából, elsőre nem vetődött el a támadó cselére, Krasznopir aztán estében lőtt, de erre a lövésre odaért a magyar kapus. A magyar válogatott az utolsó pillanatokig támadott, előbb Jurek megpattanó lövését kellett kiütnie Rizniknek, majd Kerkez kísérletét kellett hárítania. A meccs utolsó perceiben az érezhető feszültség kipattant, egymásnak az estek a két csapat játékosai, miután kiállították Nazarenkót a 92. percben. Szoboszlait az egész meccs alatt, sokszor alattomosan faragták, és ez nem egyszer büntetlenül maradt a bíró részéről. Most Cihankovval szólalkoztak össze, majd Kerkez került közéjük, és vele kezdődött a tülekedés. Aztán mindenki ott termett, és a nézőtérről mindenféle tárgyat kezdtek el bedobálni a futballistákra és a stábtagokra. Végül sikerült a játékosokat lecsillapítani, Szoboszlai kapott egy sárgát, így folytatódhatott a játék. A magyar válogatott még ezután is mindent megtett az egyenlítésért, de nem járt sikerrel. A válogatott legközelebb hétfőn játszik majd Nemzetek Ligája-meccset Észak-Írországgal. Szoboszlai Dominik az M4 Sportnak nyilatkozott rögtön a meccs után, és azt mondta, hogy egy olyan kakaskodás, ami végén volt, benne van a fociban. „Kiraktunk mindent, a szerencse nem volt velünk, nem ment be semmi” – mondta a csapatkapitány, aki szerint Ukrajnának nem sok köze volt a második félidőben a mérkőzéshez, majd megint utalt a meccs végi jelentekre. „Volt egy ilyen szituáció, de ez egy jó jel arra, hogy mindegy ki van ott bele fogunk állni. Folytatni kell amit csinálni, és mellénk fog állni a szerencse” – mondta rövid értékelésében. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Savannah Blake/The Gazette CEDAR RAPIDS — It’s hard to say what’s more difficult for rookies at Cedar Rapids Fire Station No. 5: learning to back the fire engine into the attached garage or figuring out how to flush the first-floor toilet. Both tasks seem easy … until it’s your turn. The apparatus bay, built with the rest of the station in 1957, is too small for modern firefighting equipment and backing the fire engine into the station — between stopped traffic on Wilson Avenue SW — risks losing a side mirror. The toilet seems simpler but, as the experienced firefighters attest, it “has its own rhythm,” and successive, well-timed flushes are needed to clear the bowl. Firefighters could try using the bathroom upstairs instead, but they risk the door sticking shut if it’s humid outside. Cedar Rapids firefighter/paramedic Justin Gibbs (left) holds on as firefighter/paramedic Cody Oberfoell drives Fire Engine No. 5 to a call in Cedar Rapids on Oct. 1. Savannah Blake/The Gazette “It’s not something you’d let go at your own personal house, but the building is just so outdated,” said firefighter and paramedic Justin Gibbs. “The facilities department comes and does their best, but some of what they’re dealing with is beyond repair.” The city hopes to address those issues and others in a $60 million bond referendum Cedar Rapids voters will find on their Nov. 3 ballot. The measure needs a 60% supermajority to pass. If approved, the funding would support the relocation, remodeling or reconstruction of six of the department’s nine stations and add a new training center — changes leaders say are needed to improve citywide response times and firefighter safety. The bond issue, if approved, would add an estimated maximum of $24.46 in property taxes per year for a home valued at $100,000 (or roughly $2.03 per month per $100,000 of property), city officials have said. A Gazette reporter recently shadowed a crew at Station No. 5 to see how current conditions affect firefighters’ day-to-day work and what effect the bond funding — if approved — would have on future operations. Bond Language The Cedar Rapids fire bond will appear on voters’ Nov. 3 ballot as Public Measure D using the following language. If approved, paying off the bonds would increase annual property tax payments by up to $24.46 per $100,000 of assessed residential property value. Shall the following public measure be adopted? Shall the City of Cedar Rapids, State of Iowa, issue its General Obligation Bonds or Capital Loan Notes in an amount not exceeding the amount of $60,000,000, in one or more series, for the purpose of paying costs of designing, constructing, reconstructing, enlarging, improving, equipping and furnishing fire stations and emergency response facilities, with related site improvements, consistent with the Cedar Rapids Fire Department Facility Plan, including but not limited to a new training facility, relocating Stations 2 and 8, remodeling Stations 4 and 9, rebuilding Stations 5 and 6, and the acquisition of real estate therefor, and acquiring new fire trucks and related emergency response equipment? ‘A lot of history’ Constructed in 1957, Station No. 5 is one of the oldest operating facilities in the department’s inventory. It sits at 509 Wilson Ave. SW and is nicknamed “Czech Town Express” for its proximity to the Czech Village neighborhood. Capt. Colton Dall told The Gazette that it’s a building with “a lot of history” as shown by the lineup of old photos on the walls and architectural artifacts like the three-story hose tower firefighters used decades ago to dry hoses after calls. The station has one of the highest call volumes in the city — a point of pride for its crews — and is staffed by a rotation of three-person, 24-hour shifts. Dall leads one such shift, joined by firefighters Gibbs and Cody Oberfoell. It’s a workplace, the trio said, but also a sort of second home for the men and women who work there. “We take a lot of pride in our station, and I think that’s true throughout the city for the most part,” Oberfoell said. “It’s almost a little bit of a friendly competition sometimes because each district wants to be the best.” Cedar Rapids Fire Department Station No. 5 Capt. Colton Dall (left), firefighter/paramedic Cody Oberfoell (center) and firefighter/paramedic Justin Gibbs serve themselves dinner after responding to a call in Cedar Rapids. Gibbs said the station’s three-person shifts try to eat dinner together and take time for fellowship. Savannah Blake/The Gazette Still, it’s not without its faults. It’s a squeeze to fit the fire engine into the existing apparatus bay, which holds one fire engine and the department’s boat for water rescue and response. Turnout gear hangs in the back of the bay, where it’s exposed to exhaust fumes and other contaminants that shorten its useful life. Water damage stains the basement floors of Cedar Rapids Fire Station No. 5, as seen in August 2026. Damage to the station, built in 1957, has required maintenance for water leaks, roof repairs and tuckpointing. Michael Baniewicz/The Gazette And the station’s multistory construction means the bedrooms and communal bathroom are on the second floor while the living room, kitchen and apparatus bay are on the main level. The gym is in the basement, where a fan frequently runs to dry out wet spots from leaking pipes. That three floors mean firefighters are frequently rushing up or down stairs when a call comes in, slowing response times and introducing fall risks. “You’ll be upstairs when a call comes in at two in the morning, and you have to get out of bed and get to the stairs while it’s dark and you’re still rubbing the sleep out of your eyes,” Dall said. “It just adds onto those response times.” Space constraints And Station No. 5 is not alone. Space is at a premium at all six of the bond-affected stations: St ation No. 2, 442 50th Ave. Court SW, slated for relocation. Station No. 4, 3600 42nd Ave. SE, remodeling planned. Station No. 5, 509 Wilson Ave. SW, slated to be rebuilt. Station No. 6, 2416 Mount Vernon Road SE, slated to be rebuilt. Station No. 8, 100 Wiley Blvd. SW, slated for relocation. Station No. 9, 415 Broderick Drive SE, remodeling planned. Station Nos. 5 and 6 are multistory designs built in 1957 while the remaining are one-story structures that opened in the ’80s as a “temporary” solution to the city’s rapid growth. All were built to accommodate the smaller firefighting equipment of decades past. “Even though this is an older station, we take pride in it. We try to sweep every day, mop every day and take care of our equipment,” Dall said. “But at the end of the day, it’s 70 years old. The bays are the same size, but the engines are a lot larger and have a lot more equipment.” Firefighter/paramedic Justin Gibbs holds onto equipment while riding to a call Oct. 1 in Cedar Rapids. Gibbs is stationed at Fire Station No. 5, 509 Wilson Ave. SW, one of the busiest stations in the city. Savannah Blake/The Gazette Doors for the apparatus bay at Station No. 6 were replaced to accommodate a modern firetruck, and even then, it’s a tight fit. Meanwhile, the crews at Station No. 8 can’t fully open the engine doors without hitting the garage walls. Station No. 2 has its gym equipment inside the garage. The exercise area at Station No. 4 is squeezed into a small room at the back of the apparatus bay, eliminating any buffer between workout spaces and engine exhaust. The bond measure, if approved, would address those issues by reconstructing Station Nos. 5 and 6, remodeling Stations Nos. 4 and 9 at their current sites, and replacing Stations Nos. 2 and 8 at new locations better equipped to handle modern call volumes and reduce response times. In an Aug. 21 media tour, Brent Smith, the newly appointed fire chief in Cedar Rapids, discusses how storing firefighting gear in the garage of Fire Station No. 6 damages the equipment and reduces its service life. Michael Baniewicz/The Gazette “Workflow matters (at fire stations), just like in a typical office,” Fire Chief Brent Smith said during a tour of the stations. “When things are flowing right, you have a good day and everything just works better. We want that for our firefighters. We don’t want the quarters they’re in to limit the work they do.” The new stations would all use a single-story design with modernized workout areas and living quarters and a drive-thru apparatus bay. That means vehicles could enter and exit through different doors, so crews wouldn’t have to stop street traffic to back into the space. Simultaneously, the relocation of Stations Nos. 2 and 8 will better align those facilities with the city’s current population and development to improve response times now and into the future as growth continues on the city’s southwest side. CRFD Fire Stations The City of Cedar Rapids this fall will ask voters to approve a $60 million general obligation bond to support a wide swath of facilities improvements for the city’s fire department. The department currently has nine fire stations spread out across the city, many of which are reaching the end of their useful life. Source: City of Cedar Rapids Fire Department . Cancer risk reduction The bond issue also focuses on reducing firefighter cancer risk through better station design, formally known as “cancer risk reducing zoning,” given that firefighters are 9% more likely to be diagnosed with cancer than the overall public, according to the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health. “Firefighters go into the good, the bad and the ugly in this city, and then they track it back with their shoes or boots, and it ends up here (at the stations),” Smith said. “And we want to address that.” Ideally, he said, fire stations have three zones: Hot zones where contaminant levels are highest, such as the apparatus garage, and warm zones, like showers and locker rooms, that act as a buffer into the contamination-free, cold zone living quarters. Firefighters’ gear sits in lockers in the garage of Fire Station No. 8 on Aug. 21, 2026, at Cedar Rapids Fire Department Station No. 8, 100 Wiley Blvd. SW in Cedar Rapids. The station, built in 1986, would be relocated if voters approve the $60 million bond referendum on the Nov. 3 ballot to improve response times in the rapidly growing southwest quadrant. Michael Baniewicz/The Gazette That cancer-risk zoning guidance came out about 20 years ago, which was too late to affect the design of older stations. Instead, firefighters at those stations walk directly from the apparatus bays into their dining room or other living areas. New station designs would implement more robust risk-reduction measures to address those concerns and reflect the design at updated stations like the main station on First Avenue East and Station No. 3 at 3520 Crestwood Drive NW. “Obviously, we all signed up for this job, and we know there’s that inherent risk for cancer,” said Gibbs, who joined the department seven years ago. “But whatever we can do on our side to (reduce that), we’d like to.” Cedar Rapids firefighter/paramedic Cody Oberfoell cleans the Station No. 5 fire engine after an Oct. 1 call. Station Capt. Colton Dall said firefighters take pride in their station and make sure the fire truck and other equipment is clean and ready to go. Savannah Blake/The Gazette Training needs Also included in the bond language is funding for additional firefighting vehicles and a new, full-feature training facility to replace the department’s existing drill tower off Third Street NW in the Time Check neighborhood.
